Expenditure on health care
*181. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the expenditure on health care in percentage
of GDP has been declining, whereas health
care needs have grown steadily over the
years; and
(b) the steps taken to raise the
Central and State health outlays
appropriately in view of the emerging
new challenges to health and to ensure
adequate health care facilities in all
parts of the country?
AIDS/HIV among the age group
of 12—25
*182. SHRI LAJPAT RAI: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the estimated number of AIDS/HIV
positive women and men in the age group
of 12—25 as on 1st January, 2000 in the
country;
(b) the number of deaths because of this
disease during the past three years,
year-wise, State-wise; and
(c) the steps taken to minimise the
casualities and the results thereof?
Selection of communities for inclusion
in ST list
*183. SHRI URKHAO GWRA
BRAHMA: Will the Minister of TRIBAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the policy of inclusion of
communities or group of people in the
Scheduled Tribe list is a continuous process;
(b) whether Government takes the
decision according to the recommendations
of the concerned State Government,
Registrar General of India and National SC/
ST Commission;
(c) the manner in which Government
can ensure that the concerned authorities
adhere to the basic criteria in the selection or
recommendation process; and
(d) the present number of communities
or groups demanding inclusion in the ST
list in the country?

WIN2\SESSION\4055RS 56
Control on population
*184. DR. ABRAR AHMED:
SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have assessed
the impact of various family planning
measures adopted to control the population
explosion in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government propose to
introduce new methods adopted in foreign
countries in the field of family planning; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Investment by companies in Uttar
Pradesh
*185. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the details of investment made in the
public and private sector in the State of Uttar
Pradesh during the last three years; and
(b) the details of projects on which
private companies/multinational companies
invested in the State during this period?
Advertisements on social themes
*186. SHRI S.S. CHANDRAN: Will
the Minister of INFORMATION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the advertisements, carrying social themes
like population control, AIDS awareness,
etc. are being telecast only in Hindi even by
regional telecasting centres;
(b) if so, why the important messages
carrying such advertisements are not shown
in the respective regional languages to bring
more awareness among the people;
(c) the action taken by Government to
telecast such advertisements in the regional
languages; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Infection in Gastrointestinal Unit of
G.B. Pant Hospital
*187. SHRI SURESH KALMADI: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that surgeries were
carried on in the Gastrointestinal Unit of the
G.B. Pant Hospital in New Delhi instead of
the operation theatre;
(b) if so, the reasons for the same;
(c) whether it is a fact that the operation
theatre has been found to be infected;
(d) whether any inquiry has been
undertaken on the subject;
(e) if so, the details of the reports in this
regard; and
(f) the steps taken by Government to
improve the cleanliness in this Hospital?
NEC Amendment Bill, 1998
*188. DR. ARUN KUMAR SARMA:
Will the Minister of DEVELOPMENT OF
NORTH EASTERN REGION be pleased
to refer to answer to Unstarred Question
4800 given in the Rajya Sabha on 13th May,
2002 and state:
(a) whether Government have obtained
the views of concerned Ministries regarding
NEC Amendment Bill, 1998;
(b) if so, the target set for introducing
the Bill; and
(c) if not, the action taken to obtain the
views and the time schedule finalized in this
regard?

Workers affected by closing of
industries
1196. SHRI C.O. POULOSE: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the Industrial units closed down
during the period 1996 to 2001, State-wise
and year-wise; and
(b) the number of workers affected by
the closing down of these units alongwith
details thereof?
Steps to assist the ailing Tea Industry
1197. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned,
"Darjeeling in Act will help Tea Industry",
which appeared in the Asian Age, dated the
10th October, 2002;
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
and
(c) the steps proposed to address the
problem highlighted in the news-item, so
as to assist the ailing Tea Industry to
compete with neighbouring tea producing
countries like Sri Lanka and Nepal?
WTO Summit at Doha
†1198. SHRI BALKAVI BAIRAGI:
PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the USA has
expressed its inability to provide concession
on the import of garments in the WTO
Summit held last year in Doha, which is a
deep shock for India and other developing
countries;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
ongoing negotiations to enter the American
markets are likely to be affected as a result
of USA decision; and
(c) if so, the action taken by Government
to resolve the problem alongwith the details
thereof?

WIN2\SESSION\4057RS 264
Relief package to Coffee growers
1199. SHRI PRASANTA CHATTERJEE:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
liberalise the credit package i.e. Liberal
Export Credit, higher moratorium period and
simpler norms for fresh loans for the Coffee
growers;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether this would help to provide
relief to the beleaguered Coffee plantation;
and
(d) the steps taken to monitor the situation
for implementation of the package?
Steering Committee on FDI
1200. SHRI J. CHITHARANJAN:
SHRI V.V. RAGHAVAN:
SHRI  AIMADUDDIN   AHMED
KHAN (DURRU):
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Tenth Plan Steering
Committee on FDI headed by Shri N.K.
Singh has proposed some measures to
attract more FDI into the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the decisions taken by Government
thereon?
India's petition against huge subsidy
provided by USA
†1201. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India has filed
petition in the WTO against the huge subsidy
being provided by the USA;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the issues
objected to by India; and
(c) by when a decision in the matter is
likely to be taken by the WTO?
Differences between India and EU on
trade issues
†1202. SHRI RAJIV RANJAN
SINGH 'LALAN':
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a controversial
situation has arisen between India and
European countries on some issues relating
to trade;
(b) if so, the details of the issues and the
views of India and European Countries on
these issues; and
(c) the steps taken to eliminate the
controversies on these issues?
Import of sensitive items
1203. SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the import of 300 sensitive
items being monitored by his Ministry
declined by 3.72 per cent in April, 2002 to
Rs. 688 crore as against Rs. 714 crore in the
corresponding month last year;
(b) if so, the main reasons for the same;
and
(c) the steps proposed in this regard?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Trade gap
1204. SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
SHRI SURESH PACHOURI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the value of exports and imports
during the first half of the current financial
year and the trade gap;
(b) the details of comparison with the
same period of 1999-2000 and 2000-2001;
and
(c) the measures taken by Government
to reduce the trade gap?
